extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in NLP/computational linguistics working on clickbait detection, dataset creators, and analysts of Spanish news headlines
extracted.subtask_description: Revising the definition of clickbait (identifying the curiosity gap as the key distinguishing feature) and proposing a methodology for creating a Spanish clickbait detection dataset (TA1C), including annotation criteria and evaluation baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait definition (curiosity gap)
rubrics_metrics.description: "clickbait is a technique for generating headlines and teasers that deliberately omit part of the information with the goal of raising the readers' curiosity, capturing their attention and enticing them to click."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revised definition centers the creation of a 'curiosity gap' as the key concept; it is intended to distinguish clickbait from other headline phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish clickbait from related phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: The creation of a curiosity gap is the key concept that distinguishes clickbait from other related phenomena such as sensationalism and headlines that do not deliver what they promise or diverge from the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When labeling or detecting clickbait, explicitly differentiate items that are merely sensational or misleading in content-delivery from those that intentionally omit information to provoke clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine concept limits and annotation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: "We introduce a new approach to clickbait detection datasets creation, by refining the concept limits and annotations criteria, minimizing the subjectivity in the decision as much as possible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset creators should clearly define the boundaries of 'clickbait' (based on the curiosity-gap definition) and produce annotation guidelines designed to reduce subjective judgment; this is a core procedural standard for dataset construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual annotation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: TA1C is composed of tweets that are "manually annotated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual annotation is used to ensure human judgment aligned with the refined criteria; training/qualification of annotators and annotation protocols are implied parts of quality control (though not detailed in the abstract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-annotator agreement as dataset quality metric (Fleiss' K)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TA1C dataset reached a 0.825 Fleiss' K inter annotator agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report inter-annotator agreement (e.g., Fleiss' K) to quantify annotation consistency; high agreement (e.g., ~0.825) is presented as evidence of reduced subjectivity and dataset reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: TA1C "consists of 3,500 tweets coming from 18 well known media sources."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset composition (size, number of sources, source reputability) should be reported to support representativeness and reproducibility; including diverse, well-known media sources is implied to be a best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source release
rubrics_metrics.description: TA1C is described as "the first open source dataset for clickbait detection in Spanish."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making datasets publicly available (open-source) is presented as a standard for enabling reproducibility and further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection model evaluation metric (F1-score)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We implement strong baselines that achieve 0.84 in F1-score."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard classification metrics such as F1-score to evaluate clickbait detection systems; baseline performance provides a reference point for future models.
